01 · About Me

About me.

The Hook

Administrative and Executive Support professional with a strong foundation in calendar and inbox management, documentation, project coordination, communication, research, and digital productivity tools. Over the past several months I've completed a hands-on Executive Assistant training program — covering calendar and travel coordination, CRM management, and executive communication — which has helped me build the judgment needed to support busy executives, not just complete tasks.

The Story

As a Licensed Criminologist, my education strengthened my analytical thinking, attention to detail, and discipline. My administrative internship at NICA-CALABARZON gave me hands-on experience in document preparation, records management, and maintaining confidentiality. Completing Google Workspace and Virtual Assistant skills assessments further strengthened my organization, research, and digital productivity skills.

The Promise

I provide reliable, organized, and proactive support — communicating clearly and adapting quickly to new systems. My goal is to help the people I support stay organized, protect their time, and operate with confidence.

How I Organized a Small Business's Digital Workspace

Client
Small Business

Practice Project

How I Coordinated a 3-Day International Executive Trip

Client
Simulated Client
Duration
3-day trip planning
Problem

A business trip to Singapore included a red-eye arrival with only a short buffer before the executive's first meeting. I needed to make sure the schedule was realistic and that there was enough time between arrival and the first commitment.

Solution

I reviewed the travel schedule, calculated the actual arrival time and available buffer, and compared it with a previous trip. I identified the main scheduling concern, presented practical options, and determined which timing questions were routine and did not need to be escalated.

Result

Created a complete 3-day itinerary with realistic timing and clear scheduling decisions, while addressing potential travel issues before they became problems.

Practice Project

How I Managed Executive Calendar Conflicts Across Time Zones

Client
Simulated Client
Duration
1-Week Calendar Management Simulation
Problem

The executive's calendar had several overlapping meeting requests, including a time-zone error that would have placed a client call at midnight. An internal meeting also conflicted with a new external request.

Solution

I reviewed the conflicts based on priority, protected existing commitments, looked for alternative times, and escalated situations that required the executive's decision instead of making the decision on their behalf.

Result

Resolved the calendar conflicts, removed double-bookings, and ensured all meetings were scheduled correctly across time zones.
